newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria says works for peace in Western Sahara.
newsitem.headline: Algeria says works for peace in Western Sahara.

text.p: Algeria is working to help bring about a peaceful solution to the Western Sahara conflict and encourages all direct contact between the Polisario Front and Morocco, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Friday.
It quoted War Veterans Minister Said Abadou as saying: "Today it is more than ever necessary to deploy more efforts ... to relaunch the peace (plan)."

Abadou was in the Saharan refugee camp in the Algerian town of Tindouf attending Thursday's celebration of the 21st anniversary of the proclamation of the Saharan Arab Democratic Republic in the territory claimed by Morocco.
A U.N. peace plan has been blocked in a dispute between the autonomy-seeking Polisario Front and Morocco over who should be allowed to vote in a referendum on the future of the territory.
The ballot is to decide whether the former Spanish colony should be independent as sought by Polisario, or be part of Morocco.
"Algeria's attachment and support for the legitimate claims of the Saharan people are firmer than ever," Abadou was quoted as saying.
Algeria's backing for the Polisario has long soured relations with neighbouring Morocco.
